summary: London cash opens at 08:00 GMT (16:00 SGT). UK CPI is due an hour earlier. Asia’s early rebound faded in the Reuters snapshot despite NVIDIA’s strong revenue forecast; no verified European opening prices or fresh sector panel are claimed.

claims.text: London is scheduled for regular 18 November cash trading, 08:00–16:30 GMT. The opening alert target is 15:00 SGT (07:00 GMT); cash opens 16:00 SGT. No current cash opening observation is claimed.
ONS schedules October CPI at 07:00 GMT (15:00 SGT). The public release page still said not yet published when checked; no actual figure or consensus surprise was verified at cutoff.

Reuters’ 18 November Asia snapshot: MSCI ex-Japan −0.1%, Nikkei −0.3%, S&P E-mini +0.3%. Its article began at 01:46 UTC; the quote time was not independently established. These are earlier mixed regional and futures observations, not European cash or final Asian marks.

claims.text: SGX regular cash is scheduled to open at 09:00 SGT on 18 November; the cash market had not opened at cutoff. This dedicated web report is covered by the daily Telegram digest, with no separate normal Singapore opening alert.

Reuters reported NYSE decliners beating advancers 3.76 to one; Nasdaq had 1,273 rises versus 3,527 falls. Software and banks underperformed. These are cash-session observations, not after-hours breadth.

After cash closed, NVIDIA reported fiscal Q3 FY2027 revenue of US$115.8 billion (+103% year on year), including US$107.6 billion Data Center revenue. GAAP gross margin was 74.8%; GAAP diluted EPS US$2.70. The company says Vera Rubin NVL72 has shipped. This is issuer reporting, not independent verification of end-user installations.

NVIDIA’s Q4 FY2027 outlook includes an extra week: revenue US$130 billion ±3%, no assumed China Data Center compute revenue, and GAAP/non-GAAP gross margins between 71% and 72%. Estimates are forward-looking; reported growth does not eliminate execution, funding or licensing risks.

Reuters’ updated global report described a rebound in US futures and a Korean technology ETF after NVIDIA’s results. No independently verified live Asia futures, ETF timestamp or exchange-wide sector basket was retrieved; the ETF is not Korean cash trading.
Singapore ministries are assessing the new US semiconductor controls with companies and US authorities; no blanket local halt is established.

October NODX rose 79.8% year on year, with strong electronics and uneven vessel/pharma shipments. Exports are not equivalent to listed-company sales; the prior STI closing print remains unresolved in the linked report.

claims.text: SGX’s regular Trade at Close phase runs 17:06–17:16 SGT when an eligible closing-auction price exists; 18:16 SGT is the closing alert target.

Yahoo’s 17 November daily row lists the STI close at 5,131.97 versus 5,183.18 on 16 November, a drop of 51.21 points (0.99%). The row had no volume. An alternative lower number was published at 16:55 SGT, before the closing phase ended, and cannot establish the final close. No matching independent final print or closing breadth verified.
SGX’s 09:32 SGT snapshot showed 5,145.40 (−0.73%), with 94 advancers and 206 decliners. This was morning breadth, not closing breadth.

CNA, citing Enterprise Singapore, reported that October NODX rose 79.8% year on year; non-electronics rose 81.9% and electronics 73.9%. Ship and boat structures added S$4.8 billion against a low base; pharmaceuticals were also a major contributor. These are trade flows, not listed-company revenue.

US BIS announced tighter controls on remote access to advanced compute on 16 November. Singapore’s joint ministry statement says specified advanced semiconductor transfers to Singapore need a licence, with a conditional carve-out for eligible US-headquartered companies or ultimate parents. The ministries are assessing implementation with firms and US authorities. No issuer-level loss, blanket ban or shipment stoppage is verified.
Reuters reported weaker Asian equities led by technology in a 17 November snapshot; regional and local closes must be validated separately.

claims.text: Alliance Medinet disclosed a membership database incident, with about 110,000 members reported affected. A separate Adept Health / Doctor Anywhere incident was reported in November. title: NVIDIA after the board reports: a lower P/E, a higher bar for buying
summary: 11 November cash closed at US$173.73; an extended-hours snapshot fell to US$158.76. NVIDIA confirmed an independent investigation. A lower price does not resolve the earnings or governance risk.
material_reason: The timing and magnitude of the separate extended-hours move make the governance and earnings scenarios material for semiconductor and index exposure.

claims.text: NVIDIA’s board announced an independent investigation on 8 November, saying it had no reason at that point to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. Huang acknowledged personal misconduct that day. Claims about foreign intelligence, shipment facilitation and a separate internal relationship remain allegations. Reuters reported a late 11 November US board meeting and a request from two US senators to preserve export records. Neither a board decision nor an export violation was independently confirmed at this review.

Media allege a foreign intelligence link and facilitation of at least US$7.5bn of chip shipments; the amount and connection are unverified here. The company’s 8 November statement was a preliminary assessment. The senators’ reported preservation request is not a legal finding.

The US cash close was US$173.73 on 11 November (+2.87% from US$168.89), after two down sessions from US$186.64 on 6 November. Stock Analysis recorded US$158.76 at 19:59 EST on 11 November (08:59 SGT on 12 November), down 8.62% from the cash close. This was extended-hours trading, which can overstate the move. Reported cash volume on 10 November was about 429 million shares, 2.4 times the 6 November volume of 180 million in the same series. The cash close remained about 20% below the 50-session SMA (US$217.12) and 15% below the 200-session SMA (US$204.47). The 10 November low of US$165.89 is a test, not a floor; a regular-session recovery above the 11 November high near US$177.54 would improve the near-term picture. A cash close below US$165.89 with unusually heavy volume would strengthen the breakdown case.

NVIDIA reported Q2 FY27 revenue of US$96.2bn (+106% year on year), including US$89.0bn in Data Center (+117%, about 92.5% of total), a 75.0% GAAP gross margin and US$2.46 diluted GAAP EPS. Its August guidance of US$108bn ±2% for Q3 assumed no China Data Center compute revenue. That makes a direct hit to the old guidance less automatic; broader controls, customer delays and key-person risk still matter.

Four published quarterly GAAP diluted EPS figures (US$1.30, US$1.76, US$2.39, US$2.46) sum to US$7.91. That implies 22.0× trailing GAAP P/E at US$173.73 and 20.1× at US$158.76. The vendor’s 14.35× forward P/E at the cash close implies roughly US$12.11 in estimated EPS, 53% above trailing EPS; its exact period and adjustment basis were not independently verified. Historical GAAP EPS can include investment gains and other non-operating items. A falling price reduces the quoted multiple only if the EPS denominator holds.

TSMC reported NT$586.89bn in October revenue (+59.7% year on year). This does not identify NVIDIA wafer or packaging allocation. CoreWeave reported over 1.7 GW of active power and raised the low end of its FY26 capex range to US$37–39bn; its expected deposits and prepayments are not collected cash. No separate new NVIDIA HBM allocation, advanced packaging deliveries, rack completion, networking shipments, power procurement, generation or cooling capacity was verified. Follow funded orders through shipment, utilization and collections; test overbuild and financing exposure.

Research stance: WATCH / wait for confirmation. The multiple is more attractive if earnings rise as expected, but it does not establish a margin of safety if earnings estimates fall or investors assign a lower multiple. A credible board disclosure and resilient guidance, cash conversion and shipments would strengthen the case. The next scheduled earnings release is about 05:20 SGT on 18 November (17 November US time), with the call at 06:00 SGT.

causation.explanation: The selloff followed reporting on possible CEO removal, consistent with a higher governance discount.
causation.transmission: Leadership uncertainty could affect succession, regulatory relationships and valuation; broader export controls could reduce future demand.
causation.alternatives: After-hours liquidity, rate repricing, AI capex expectations and prior heavy selling can amplify moves. A board meeting is not a verdict or proof the entire price change is attributable to one headline.

title: Reported Gulf navigation strike leaves commercial impact unverified
summary: Reuters reported an attack following a 10 November claim, with no independent damage assessment. Direct Singapore impact is not established.
material_reason: Navigation infrastructure can affect transits and delivered energy costs, but damage and actual shipping effects need separate evidence.

claims.text: Iranian state media claimed a strike on navigation infrastructure on 10 November; Reuters on 11 November cited three informed sources for an attack but could not independently establish damage or verify destruction. This is a reported combat-related incident, separate from routine drills and diplomacy. No local aviation, cargo, cyber or energy loss was established. Sustained transit or insurance disruption could increase Singapore/Asian bunker, freight, jet fuel and import costs; traffic can also hold up via alternate routes and inventories. Check operator notices, verified transit and premiums on 12–13 November; unchanged flows and costs would weaken the spillover case.

causation.explanation: Verified disruption to navigation could reduce safe passage.
causation.transmission: If persistent, extra routing or insurance costs can reach Singapore bunkers, aviation fuel and Asian supply chains. No actual local interruption or associated cyber event was verified.
causation.alternatives: Operators can maintain flows via redundancy, alternate routes or inventories; energy price changes can also reflect demand.

claims.text: The original Binance30 October security update was retrieved at20:07:29SGT; its displayed initial02:23/updated11:36 clocks have no verified timezone, so no precise original UTC publication time is inferred. Binance estimates total impact aroundUS$6.3bn and aboutUS$3bn frozen on-chain. These are issuer estimates, not audited final net losses. Frozen assets are not necessarily recovered, available for payment or returned to customers; subtracting the two does not establish an ultimate loss.

The updated global notice says deposits continue normally while withdrawals are temporarily suspended. It promises to cover losses from company funds and SAFU and publish an updated proof-of-reserves record after remediation. Those are company commitments, not independently verified completed reimbursement, restored withdrawals or a full assets-and-liabilities audit.

Binance Japan’s later response says its customer assets are separately managed and no impact is confirmed. Its status table reports crypto deposits/trading and fiat services operating, crypto withdrawals still suspended, with resumption expected within48hours. This supersedes the initial broader deposit suspension notice. It is a subsidiary statement, not proof of global solvency or completed restoration.

Reuters reports that TRM Labs and Chainalysis assess North Korean responsibility with high confidence, while Binance says its own investigation has not identified a responsible person. No original vendor analysis or public law-enforcement finding for this incident was independently retrieved. State attribution therefore remains an attributed assessment, not an established identity finding.

causation.alternatives: The strongest limiting explanation is containment with sufficient segregated/customer and company resources. A large gross loss estimate does not alone prove insolvency, bank contagion or customer loss; continued trading alone does not prove unrestricted settlement.

causation.explanation: Frozen funds can limit damage without being usable recovery.
causation.transmission: A verified return to the rightful entity could reduce ultimate financial impact, but legal entitlement, control, valuation and time-to-release matter. A future proof-of-reserves snapshot must be assessed together with scope, liabilities, encumbrances and subsequent events.
causation.alternatives: Assets may be released gradually, revalued or disputed, and compensation can come from separate resources. No assumed dollar-for-dollar cash recovery, net-loss figure or independently certified balance-sheet coverage is adopted.

No specific Singapore bank, broker, port, fund or public issuer loss was established.
causation.alternatives: Entity separation, limited exposure and prompt service restoration could contain the event. No individual exposure is inferred. Social-feed saturation and unrelated market moves do not quantify exposure, causation or representative sentiment.

claims.text: This is a delayed29 October closing read with actual research cutoff 2026-10-29T18:08:14Z. The16:50GMT editorial target was earlier. It is anchored to the verified LSE calendar; continental coverage remains partial. Earlier intraday STOXX extracts are not used as final closes.

Alliance News’s17:00UTC closing report gives FTSE100 at10,722.07 and FTSE250 at24,674.16, with CAC40 +1.1% and DAX40 +1.3%. Reuters’s updated London closing body independently corroborates the FTSE100 level and +0.26%. These are attributed secondary closes, not exchange-certified total returns; first-publication times are not closing-price clocks.

The actual ECB29 October decision retained its three key rates. It identifies uncertainty and energy-related inflation risks while retaining data dependence. A reported possibility of future tightening must not be rewritten as an announced commitment.

US advance Q3 real GDP grew3.4% at a seasonally adjusted annual rate, versus2.2% inQ2; private domestic final sales grew4.9%. These are quarterly annualized, revisable figures. Quarterly PCE/core inflation of2.1%/2.5% annualized is not the September year-on-year series.

AIXTRON’s9M revenue was EUR358.1m versus369.5m a year earlier despite strong Q3 order momentum. The original cash discussion says customer advances help finance production; increased liquidity also reflects convertible funding. Order growth, current revenue and finance-sourced liquidity must remain separate.

causation.explanation: Historical growth and the latest household purchasing power give different signals.
causation.transmission: Quarterly GDP can remain strong while monthly real consumption stalls; inflation affects financing, real budgets and valuation through different channels. Neither observation alone resolves the next policy decision.
causation.alternatives: Advance GDP can be revised and a single month may be noisy. Investment, inventories and sector mix can offset household weakness; no numerical causal share for an index move is established.

causation.explanation: NVIDIA / AI Infrastructure: optical networks add concrete supplier evidence.
causation.transmission: AIXTRON links laser-equipment demand to AI data-centre communications. This supports watching optical component manufacturing alongside HBM/memory, foundry/advanced packaging, racks, networking, power delivery/grid equipment, cooling and generation. It does not establish a new NVIDIA purchase, market-wide shortage or winner across every layer.
causation.alternatives: Earlier preliminary disclosure means order momentum is not wholly new today. Orders can be delayed or cancelled; customer advances and convertible financing differ from recurring customer profit. Growing capacity may relieve bottlenecks or overshoot utilization. No circular-financing conclusion follows without counterparty-level cash reconciliation.

causation.explanation: Policy holds do not settle forward rate or earnings expectations.
causation.transmission: The ECB retained its rates and data-dependent framework. The release itself does not promise a December hike. Company earnings, customer expectations and capitalization can diverge even when reported revenue rises.
causation.alternatives: Expected decisions may already be priced. FX, duration, regional weights, positioning and different quote clocks can explain reactions without a single dominant policy catalyst. A synchronized rates/FX panel remains missing.

causation.explanation: Diplomacy / humanitarian attribution: a letter is not a peace settlement.
causation.transmission: Reuters29 October reports Trump described Vance’s outreach as medical-supply assistance; other media described a bid to revive negotiations, which Reuters could not immediately verify. The letter and original Iranian response were not independently obtained. This is contested diplomatic purpose, not a new verified combat event, deployment or reopened route.
causation.alternatives: Humanitarian outreach and diplomacy could coexist. Reported intent does not establish implementation or de-escalation. For Singapore/Asia, shipping insurance, aviation routing, energy import costs, supply-chain continuity, cyber resilience and humanitarian access are conditional channels; no new direct local disruption or quantified cost is established here. Confirm with attributable official texts and operator notices, not circulating videos or an incognito-feed sample.

causation.explanation: Underlying margins, competitive guidance and valuation effects complicate headline earnings growth.

causation.explanation: Energy and haze reports have distinct local transmission channels, not a single conflict narrative.

SIA’s future fuel contract is commercial planning, not a response proven caused by a military incident.
causation.alternatives: Diplomatic reports, positioning, weather, hedges and ordinary commercial procurement may explain changes without new physical disruption. A reported negotiation approach is not a confirmed agreement or ceasefire; no tactical detail or unverified force location is used.

causation.explanation: Upcoming data and policy are a test, not a known outcome.
causation.transmission: US consumption/inflation and European policy can alter funding conditions for Singapore banks, REITs and infrastructure. Company results may confirm demand while undermining cash returns. No future GDP, rate decision or cash opening response is invented.
causation.alternatives: Revisions, composition, guidance and positioning may matter more than headline growth; a single market move cannot isolate causation. No verified new direct political/social post or representative public-opinion measure was obtained; official calendars prove planned events only.

claims.text: Calendar and cutoff: NYSE lists no scheduled holiday or early close for 27 October; core cash trading ends 16:00 New York. This read's cutoff is 16:59:54 New York / 04:59:54 Singapore on 28 October: 59m54s after scheduled cash close and 39m54s after the editorial target. It is not an auction-time observation.

Reuters reports the cash close: S&P 500 7,722.60 (+0.60%), Nasdaq Composite 26,477.81 (+1.18%), Dow 52,377.57 (+0.03%). NYSE advances/declines were 1.83:1. US volume was 16.10bn shares versus a 17.18bn recent average. Technology led sector gains; energy was weakest. These are reported closing observations, not independently downloaded exchange series.

Boeing's Q3 issuer release reports US$24.188bn revenue, GAAP loss per share US$0.26 and non-GAAP core loss US$0.34. Operating cash flow US$1.496bn less US$1.032bn capex yields US$464m non-GAAP FCF; nine-month FCF remained negative US$359m. A positive quarter does not erase cumulative cash consumption, delivery-mix or supply-chain risks.

NVIDIA/AI Infrastructure — logistics enters the beneficiary research lane. UPS CEO Carol Tome told Reuters she sees a US$15bn annual data-centre logistics opportunity across freight, warehousing and delivery. She did not disclose current data-centre revenue. This is management's opportunity estimate, not UPS booked revenue, secured backlog, a new NVIDIA order or proof of a bottleneck shifting.

After-hours evidence, separate from the cash close: Reuters reports Visa fiscal Q4 net revenue of US$12.1bn (+13%), net income US$6bn and EPS US$3.19. Payments volume grew 9%; cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe grew 14%. The report observed shares down more than 1% in extended trading. Growth in nominal network spending is not a direct measure of real household purchasing power.

Robinhood's issuer release, distributed at 16:05 New York, reports Q3 revenue US$1.42bn (+12%), diluted EPS US$0.51 (-16%) and adjusted EPS US$0.60 (-3%). Crypto revenue fell 55% while options and equities revenue rose. These post-close results cannot explain the earlier cash close; trading volumes, customer deposits, revenue and profit are different economic measures.

Earlier primary evidence retained with its original access time: Coca-Cola's Q3 release showed global unit-case volume growth of 5% while North America was flat. Its refresh and the UPS primary release refresh were inaccessible in this pass. This is a reused quarterly observation, not a new overnight consumer-demand finding.

Reuters' updated oil report gives settlements of Brent US$113.88/barrel (-1.67%) and WTI US$99.90 (-1.83%). Earlier intraday quotations differ and are not substituted for settlement. The extract does not identify both delivery months, so the marks are not used for a front-month/forward-curve comparison.

Shared conflict risk review — event/report date 27 October. Reuters attributes the Saudi refinery-strike/fire claim to the Houthis and says Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed that strike. Separate reporting about a contained terminal-area fire does not independently establish attacker, refinery damage or lost output. No new direct Singapore casualty, shipment interruption or infrastructure outage is established in these sources.

Official next evidence: the FOMC calendar lists a 27–28 October meeting; no October decision was posted on the retrieved calendar. SK hynix schedules its release before 09:00 Seoul on 28 October and call at 09:00 Seoul / 08:00 Singapore. Expectations and invitations are not policy outcomes or earnings results.

causation.explanation: NVIDIA/AI Infrastructure — bull and bear interpretations of logistics exposure.

claims.text: The NYSE calendar lists 23 October as a regular Friday trading day; the 2026 calendar shows no holiday or early-close marker for that date.

On 23 October the S&P 500 closed at 7,623.68 (-0.52%), the Dow at 52,215.16 (-1.23%), the Nasdaq Composite at 25,955.34 (-0.21%) and the Russell 2000 at 2,775.90 (-0.29%). AP reported nearly three quarters of S&P 500 constituents declined.

Reuters reported the S&P 500 technology sector rose 0.4% and energy rose 2.5% to a record high; Brent settled at $116.72 (+3.14%) and WTI at $103.27 (+3.8%). The US 10-year Treasury yield rose 3.7 basis points to 4.99%. These reports describe concurrent market moves, not proof that one event caused each sector return.

Reuters said telecom shares including Verizon fell after a report that SpaceX was discussing a US wireless-carrier program, and American Express fell 3.7% after its results and a reported efficiency plan. These are company or subsector observations, not full sector returns.

President Donald Trump (Republican, U.S. president) wrote on Truth Social at 11:40 ET on 22 October: “Iran is doing everything they can to drive up the price of Oil prior to the U.S. Midterm Election.” This records his statement only; the assertion about Iranian intent is unverified and is not evidence of market causation or public opinion.

The White House published a presidential proclamation on 23 October modifying which Canadian products face additional 50% duties; the changes are scheduled to apply from 30 October. This is an enacted policy watchpoint, not an identified cause of Friday's index moves.

causation.explanation: Oil-price and supply-risk news coincided with the broad decline: AP described Brent's rise and the effects of the Iran war on supply; Reuters linked the session's energy-risk repricing to Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and an oil spill reported by UAE authorities. This supports an inflation and input-cost channel, but does not isolate a single cause of the index fall.
causation.transmission: If crude remains elevated, fuel and logistics costs can pressure consumer, airline, industrial and utility margins, while producers may benefit; higher inflation risk can also affect yields and valuation multiples.
causation.alternatives: The prior day's AI-capex repricing, earnings reactions and the SpaceX wireless-carrier report also affected technology and telecom names; index weights and company-specific news can explain part of the divergence.

causation.explanation: The session was selective rather than uniformly risk-off: Reuters reported technology and energy gains alongside losses in the major indexes, while AP reported broad S&P constituent declines.
causation.transmission: A recovery would require broader participation beyond a small number of sectors; narrow gains can leave the index vulnerable to further megacap or oil reversals.
causation.alternatives: Available closing breadth is limited to AP's broad S&P summary; NYSE/Nasdaq advance-decline counts, volume, volatility and eight sector-group closes were not independently verified.

causation.explanation: Trump's public oil-price post and the White House's tariff proclamation are relevant political signals, but neither source establishes that political messaging or the proclamation drove the 23 October market move.
causation.transmission: Oil-policy claims may shift perceived supply or escalation risk; the Canadian-duty change may matter to exposed manufacturers when it takes effect on 30 October.
causation.alternatives: Physical supply conditions, company earnings, positioning and broader inflation expectations may dominate; the direct social post is one official's sentiment signal and not representative opinion.

title: Viral war warnings: preparedness is not an imminent-war alert
summary: UK household advice, a September European security statement and Gulf shipping risk are real but distinct. None establishes the viral claim that a wider war is imminent; energy-price effects remain conditional.

claims.text: The UK announced a three-year Be Ready campaign on 22 October, advising households to prepare for three days of ordinary service disruption, including severe weather. The government says much of the advice has existed since 2024. This is not an announcement that war is imminent.

The European Commission's statement on the attempted Leipzig-Halle cargo-plane attack was dated 2 September, not a new October warning. It relayed the German government's attribution to Russia and called for infrastructure resilience.

NATO's Secretary General acknowledged hybrid attacks but said on 14 October that the alliance saw no imminent threat against NATO territory. This is an assessment at that date, not a guarantee about future events.

Gulf maritime danger is not imaginary: the US maritime advisory describes continued threats and attacks on commercial vessels. The IEA's 14 October report says crude flows had partly recovered while tanker attacks, freight costs and constrained refined products kept the recovery fragile. It does not support a guaranteed fall in oil prices from a claimed US policy move.

causation.explanation: The clips splice different dates and risk categories into one urgent narrative.
causation.transmission: Routine household preparedness, a dated European sabotage statement and a live Gulf shipping risk warrant monitoring, but do not by themselves establish a timetable for wider war. For markets, verified shipping incidents and energy supply, freight and insurance costs are the channels to test, particularly for Asian fuel importers, transport and industry.
causation.alternatives: Escalation could occur despite the current NATO assessment; conversely, diplomacy or safer passage could ease risk. The evidence here does not quantify either probability.

scenarios.name: Risk persists without a wider war
scenarios.outcome: Shipping and fuel costs remain elevated or volatile while household preparedness remains general advice.
scenarios.trigger: Maritime advisories and IEA data continue to show threats and constrained products without a new official alliance alert.
scenarios.invalidation: A new, corroborated military escalation or an official change in threat assessment alters the premise.
scenarios.horizon: Next seven days; reassess on material official updates.

scenarios.name: Energy pressure eases conditionally
scenarios.outcome: Sustained safer shipping and restored refined-product flows could reduce cost pressure; lower consumer fuel prices would not be automatic or immediate.
scenarios.trigger: Verified vessel traffic, freight and product-supply series improve together.
scenarios.invalidation: Further attacks, infrastructure damage or renewed stock draws offset crude export gains.
scenarios.horizon: Next several weeks; use fresh IEA and maritime updates.

watchpoints.signal: Check official NATO/EU assessments and Gulf maritime advisories against new short-form claims; compare IEA crude, refined-product and freight evidence.
watchpoints.confirms: New official evidence substantiates a changed threat assessment or measurable supply disruption.
watchpoints.contradicts: The claim relies on recycled footage, generic preparedness guidance or price predictions without fresh primary evidence.

material_reason: Several circulating clips connect UK preparedness, European security and Gulf energy into an imminent-world-war claim. A calm, source-dated correction matters to readers and to energy-sensitive industries; this report does not reproduce tactical details or make a trading recommendation.
